title: Conducting Regulatory Investigations: From Referral to Outcome
summary: An eight-module practitioner programme taking enforcement staff through a regulatory investigation, from referral and powers to compelled interviews, findings and outcome.
intro: This training programme equips enforcement staff to run regulatory investigations from referral to outcome: scoping cases, using information-gathering powers, handling evidence, interviewing under compulsion and reaching fair, robust decisions.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give investigators and case teams a practical, step-by-step method for conducting regulatory investigations that are focused, fair and capable of withstanding challenge. Participants leave able to scope and plan a case, gather and review evidence, conduct compelled interviews, prepare findings and warning notices, and feed lessons back into supervision.
sections.What It Covers: Case selection and referral, scoping and investigation planning, information-gathering powers, evidence handling and document review, interviews under compulsion, findings and warning notices, settlement and decision-making, and lessons for supervision.
Intended Audience: Enforcement investigators, case managers and lawyers
Supervisory staff seconded to or working alongside enforcement teams
Staff moving into enforcement from supervision, authorisation or other agencies
Learning Objectives: Apply case selection criteria and assess referrals consistently
Scope and plan an investigation with clear hypotheses, milestones and resources
Use information-gathering powers lawfully, proportionately and effectively
Handle, review and analyse evidence to an evidential standard
Plan and conduct compelled interviews that are fair and productive
Prepare robust findings, manage settlement and feed lessons back into supervision
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a four-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. The modules follow the life of a single case, combining short briefings with a running investigation exercise, interview role-play and a mock case conference, and can be selected or tailored to the authority's powers and procedures.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of enforcement, supervision or legal casework is helpful. No prior investigative training is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO (2015), Credible Deterrence in the Enforcement of Securities Regulation
IOSCO (2017), Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation
IOSCO (2016), Enhanced Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding Concerning Consultation and Cooperation and the Exchange of Information

modules.title: Case Selection and Referral
modules.summary: How cases reach enforcement, how referrals are assessed and how the authority decides which matters merit a formal investigation.
objectives: Assess a referral against the authority's case selection criteria
Distinguish matters for investigation from supervisory or alternative outcomes
Record the rationale for opening or declining a case
syllabus: Sources of cases: supervision, whistleblowers, complaints and market surveillance
Case selection criteria: seriousness, harm, deterrence and resources
Alternatives to investigation and early resolution
Documenting the referral decision

modules.title: Scoping and Planning the Investigation
modules.summary: How to define the scope of an investigation, frame hypotheses and build a plan that keeps the case focused, proportionate and on time.
objectives: Define scope, subjects and potential breaches
Build an investigation plan with hypotheses, milestones and resources
Manage scope creep, risks and stakeholder expectations
syllabus: Scoping documents and appointment of investigators
Hypotheses, elements of the breach and evidence matrices
Resourcing, timetables and case governance
Notifying subjects and managing parallel proceedings

modules.title: Information-Gathering Powers
modules.summary: The powers available to the authority to require information, documents and attendance, and how to use them lawfully and effectively.
objectives: Identify the information-gathering powers available and their limits
Draft clear and proportionate information requirements
Respond to privilege claims, non-compliance and delay
syllabus: Requirements for information, documents and attendance
Drafting notices: scope, deadlines and format
Legal professional privilege, self-incrimination and confidentiality
On-site inspections, third parties and requests to other authorities

modules.title: Evidence Handling and Document Review
modules.summary: How to collect, preserve and review large volumes of documents and data so that evidence is reliable, admissible and well organised.
objectives: Apply sound practice in evidence collection, continuity and storage
Plan and manage document review, including electronic review tools
Analyse evidence and build a chronology against the elements of the breach
syllabus: Chain of custody, forensic copies and data integrity
Electronic disclosure, search terms and review workflows
Chronologies, evidence matrices and gap analysis
Disclosure obligations and unused material

modules.title: Interviews under Compulsion
modules.summary: How to plan and conduct compelled interviews with firm staff and subjects, balancing effective questioning with the rights of the interviewee.
objectives: Plan a compelled interview strategy and question outline
Conduct interviews that are fair, structured and evidentially sound
Handle legal representatives, privilege objections and evasive answers
syllabus: Compelled and voluntary interviews: rights, cautions and use of answers
Interview planning, document bundles and questioning structure
Managing lawyers, objections and difficult interviewees
Role-play: interviewing a senior manager under compulsion

modules.title: Findings, Reports and Warning Notices
modules.summary: How to analyse the evidence against the alleged breaches, draft investigation reports and warning notices, and test the case before it goes to decision.
objectives: Assess whether the evidence establishes each element of the breach
Draft clear, balanced investigation findings and warning notices
Test the case for weaknesses and procedural risk
syllabus: Analysing evidence against the standard of proof
Structuring the investigation report and proposed findings
Warning notices, representations and access to material
Internal challenge, legal review and case conferences

modules.title: Settlement and Decision-Making
modules.summary: How cases are resolved by settlement or contested decision, how penalties are determined and how fairness and consistency are maintained.
objectives: Explain the separation of investigation and decision-making
Apply penalty frameworks and settlement principles consistently
Manage negotiations and communicate final outcomes
syllabus: Independent decision-makers and procedural fairness
Penalty frameworks: seriousness, aggravation, mitigation and discounts
Settlement negotiations, agreed facts and admissions
Final notices, publicity and appeals

modules.title: Lessons for Supervision and Case Workshop
modules.summary: How enforcement outcomes improve supervision and deterrence, followed by a mock case conference in which participants take a case from referral to recommended outcome.
objectives: Identify lessons from cases for supervisory practice and policy
Communicate outcomes to promote credible deterrence
Apply the full investigation method to a realistic case
syllabus: Feeding findings back to supervision, authorisation and policy
Credible deterrence and outcome publicity
Post-case reviews and continuous improvement
Workshop: mock case conference from referral to recommended outcome

related.title: Enforcement and Sanctions
related.summary: A ten-module programme taking enforcement and supervisory staff through the full life of an enforcement case, from triage and evidence to sanctions, settlement and cooperation.

related.title: Authorisation and Licensing: The Regulatory Gateway
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving authorisation staff a structured, defensible methodology for assessing applications, key individuals, owners and changes at the regulatory gateway.

related.title: Crisis Management and Resolution
related.summary: A ten-module programme preparing supervisors for firm and system-wide stress, from early intervention and recovery and resolution planning to crisis communication and a live simulation.

related.title: Fit and Proper Assessments: Approving Owners, Directors and Key Function Holders
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on assessing owners, controllers, directors and key function holders, from evidence gathering and interviews to defensible decisions.

related.title: Policy-Making and Rule-Making
related.summary: An eight-module programme covering the full policy cycle, from problem definition and cost-benefit analysis to drafting, standards implementation and post-implementation review.

related.title: Assessing Board Effectiveness
related.summary: An eight-module programme showing supervisors how to assess how a board really works, from papers and decisions to culture and challenge, culminating in case-study interviews.
